<WORKER-BRIEF>

**To:** `vcpolish`
**PR:** [flutter/flutter#196561](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/196561), "Fix --split-per-abi versionCode when android {} omits versionCode"
**Your branch:** `vcfix-manifest-fallback`. The last head I saw was `7233196849d`. Before you start, fetch and check that it is still the head.
**Task:** Act on audit finding 2A only. Other audit findings will reach you in separate briefs, so don't fold them into this change.

An audit agent built a playground app against this PR in 28 configurations. Here is its method note, verbatim:

> **Verification**: Every output APK in `build/app/outputs/flutter-apk/` and `build/app/outputs/apk/` was inspected with `aapt2 dump badging`.

Here is finding 2A, verbatim:

> ### 2A. Following the error message's `-P force-version-code-ignoring-abi=true` suggestion when no `versionCode` exists builds **un-installable APKs (`versionCode=''`)**
>
> When neither `android {}` nor `src/main/AndroidManifest.xml` sets a `versionCode`:
> - **Flutter 3.47**: Used `-1` (`variant.mergedFlavor.versionCode`) and silently built APKs with `versionCode='999'`, `'1999'`, `'3999'` (`1000 * abi + (-1)`).
> - **PR #196561**: Fails cleanly (big improvement!), and prints:
>   > `Set versionCode = flutter.versionCode in defaultConfig (or on each product flavor), or pass -P force-version-code-ignoring-abi=true to keep one versionCode.`
>
> > [!CAUTION]
> > **Escape-Hatch Trap**
> > If the developer follows the second suggestion on that exact project:
> > ```bash
> > flutter build apk --debug --split-per-abi -P force-version-code-ignoring-abi=true
> > ```
> > the build **exits `0`** and writes `app-armeabi-v7a-debug.apk`, `app-arm64-v8a-debug.apk`, and `app-x86_64-debug.apk` with **`versionCode=''` (empty / missing in the compiled binary `AndroidManifest.xml`)**. `adb install` rejects those APKs on Android devices. Saying *"to keep one versionCode"* when no `versionCode` exists anywhere misleads the user into producing broken APKs.

**Judge this finding on its merits; don't just obey it.** Some parts are proven and some are not:

1. **Proven by the audit's own method:** with the force flag and no `versionCode` anywhere, `aapt2` shows `versionCode=''`.
2. **Not proven:** "`adb install` rejects those APKs". The method section only mentions `aapt2 dump badging`, so no install was tested. Don't repeat that claim in code comments, the PR description or tests unless you reproduce it yourself.
3. **Separate from 1 and 2:** the wording "to keep one versionCode" is misleading when no versionCode exists. That is true however the install question turns out.

**Reproduce before you change anything:**

1. Make a fresh app. Remove `versionCode` from `android {}` / `defaultConfig` (including `flutter.versionCode`) and make sure `src/main/AndroidManifest.xml` has no `android:versionCode`.
2. On your branch, run `flutter build apk --debug --split-per-abi`. Confirm it fails with the message quoted above.
3. Run `flutter build apk --debug --split-per-abi -P force-version-code-ignoring-abi=true`. Record the exit code, then run `aapt2 dump badging` on each APK.
4. Run `adb install` on an emulator or device for at least the APK that matches its ABI. Record the exact output, whether it succeeds or fails.
5. Repeat step 3 on Flutter 3.47 (pre-PR). This tells us whether the force flag already produced empty versionCodes before this PR (a pre-existing problem that our new message now points users toward) or whether this PR caused it. Say which in your report.

**Then choose a fix.** You decide, but explain your choice. The options I can see:

- **(a)** Suggest the force flag only when a versionCode actually exists (in `android {}` or the manifest). With none, tell the user to set `versionCode = flutter.versionCode`.
- **(b)** Also fail, or warn loudly, when the force flag is set and no versionCode exists anywhere, so the escape hatch can't silently produce versionCode-less APKs.
- **(c)** Reword only. This is weakest, because the trap stays.

I lean toward (a), plus (b) if step 4 shows the APKs really are broken. If step 4 shows they install and run fine, (a) alone may be enough. Keep the change scoped to the error and suggestion path. Don't change what the force flag does when a versionCode exists.

**Tests:** Add or update unit tests in the Gradle plugin's existing test suite under `packages/flutter_tools/gradle/`, next to the tests that already cover this PR's fallback. Cover:

- no versionCode and no force flag: the message no longer offers the force flag, or offers it only with a correct caveat
- no versionCode with the force flag: the behaviour you chose for (b), if you implement it
- a versionCode exists with the force flag: unchanged

Run the plugin tests and any `flutter_tools` tests that check this message, then push.

**Push** to the `reidbaker-agent` fork branch that backs the PR, never to `flutter/flutter`. If the branch turns out to live upstream, stop and tell me before pushing. Merge; don't rebase.

**Don't post on GitHub about this finding.** The audit is internal, so there is no thread to answer. If the PR description mentions the force flag, update that text to match.

**Report back with:**

1. **Verdict on 2A:** changed, modified or declined, with reasons, covering each of points 1–3 above.
2. **Reproduction evidence:** commands, exit codes, `aapt2` lines and the exact `adb install` output, for both your branch and 3.47.
3. **Fix:** which option you picked, the new message text verbatim, and the files you touched.
4. **Tests:** what you added and the commands you ran, with pass/fail.
5. **New head SHA.**

Don't call the PR ready. I'll read the diff myself and run an adversarial review on your fix commits before anything goes to reidbaker.
